Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - apply today!

The Research Technician will support a multidisciplinary biomedical research program through the conduct of laboratory-based molecular and cellular experiments and animal studies. This position will spend a substantial portion of time assisting with animal husbandry, animal procedures, and study-related data collection. During periods when animal studies are inactive, the technician will perform a variety of laboratory techniques including cell culture, molecular biology assays, sample processing, and general laboratory support activities. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, comfortable working with laboratory animals, and interested in developing a broad range of research skills in both in vivo and in vitro settings.

Essential Functions

  • Conducts technical laboratory procedures and animal research anesthesia, surgery, and postoperative care.
  • Records experimental observations.
  • Assists in the monitoring of research laboratory inventory and equipment and taking appropriate actions.
  • Assist in maintaining the storage of research data.
  • Assists in organizing and coordinating of the daily and weekly schedule of procedures to be performed.
  • Operates all equipment and devices necessary for the performance of research procedures.
  • Assists in the maintenance of the physical environment.
  • Performs all necessary surgical procedures, data collection and storage for all GLP (Good Laboratory Practices) research studies.
  • Prepares chemical solutions as required for research projects.
  • Searches library files for articles and abstracts dealing with various projects.
  • Supports physicians and medical staff during human clinical investigations in cardiac catheterization laboratory and operating rooms.


Physical Requirements
Work in fast paced office/laboratory environment. Requires ability to sit or stand for long periods of time. Each employee has the responsibility to work in a safe manner.

Education, Experience and Certifications

High School Diploma or GED required. Bachelor's of Science Degree required or its equivalent in experience. 1 year experience in research and rehabilitation, hospital or therapy required. Nursing assistant experience preferred. Experience working with laboratory animals and perform handling procedures preferred. Experience with rodent models, cell culture, molecular biology, and AALAS certification is preferred.

In this role, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining BMC firmware for server platforms, working closely with hardware, system, and cross-functional engineering teams to deliver reliable, scalable, and high-quality BMC solutions throughout the full server lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, maintain, and debug BMC firmware based on server hardware architecture and system design requirements.
  • Perform high-level and low-level design, implementation, and integration of new BMC features and system enhancements.
  • Lead or contribute as a platform owner or domain expert, providing technical guidance and mentoring to team members.
  • Collaborate with hardware, BIOS, and system teams to bring up and port OpenBMC on custom server platforms.
  • Participate in system integration, validation, and issue root-cause analysis across the full server development cycle.

Required Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with BMC development or open-source BMC solutions (e.g., OpenBMC).
  • Strong C/C++ programming skills, with solid software design principles and code tracing/debugging capabilities.
  • Good understanding of Linux operating system architecture, including kernel and user-space applications.
  • Solid knowledge of low-level hardware protocols, including:
    I2C, PMBus, SPI, UART, JTAG, GPIO.
  • Strong understanding of IPMI 2.0 and DCMI 1.5, including:
    IPMI Messaging, SDR, SEL, FRU, SOL, IPMB, LAN, KCS, Event Log, PEF, ME, NM, PECI.
  • Ability to independently port BMC firmware to custom hardware platforms or implement platform-specific algorithms.
  • Experience participating in at least one complete server project lifecycle (from bring-up to production).
  • Experience with Redfish, WebUI, or Linux kernel development.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electronics, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience acting as a technical lead, platform owner, or domain expert in BMC-related projects.
  • Familiarity with server hardware bring-up, manufacturing diagnostics, or system validation.
  • Experience with scripting languages such as Python or Shell for automation or debugging.
  • Experience working in Agile or cross-functional development environments.
  • Strong documentation and technical communication skills.

Personal Attributes

  • Passionate about coding, debugging, and learning new technologies.
  • Pragmatic, open-minded, and solution-oriented.
  • Patient, responsible, and enthusiastic about engineering work.
  • Strong logical thinking and communication skills.
  • A team player with a willingness to mentor others and contribute beyond individual tasks.

Job Description

Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others to fulfil their potential?

Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?

Then consider the role of Employment Adviser at Reed in Partnership!

Please note, internal applications for this role close on 04/08/2026

Who we are:

Reed in Partnership's Employability Division aims to positively transform lives by helping individuals who are unemployed, economically inactive, or facing challenges such as health conditions, disabilities, or caring responsibilities to find sustainable employment. Through a wide range of tailored support services including one-to-one careers guidance, CV writing, interview preparation, and skills training, we have supported over 250,000 people on their journey into work.

Our Restart Scheme, funded by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), focuses specifically on supporting the long-term unemployed who are referred and mandated to the scheme by their local Job Centre Plus. We provide them with up to 12 months of personalised support to enter or re-enter the workforce.

What is the role about?

Employment Advisers are the front line of Reed in Partnership, directly contributing to our mission by supporting jobseekers (our participants), engaging with local employers, and promoting the benefits of the Restart Scheme within the local community. Our participants are the lifeblood of our business and providing them with an excellent service is at the very core of the Employment Adviser role.

Just some of your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Taking Ownership

  • Meeting with and supporting a caseload of long-term unemployed jobseekers, identifying their barriers and creating tailored action plans to progress them into employment.

  • Delivering personalised, one-to-one guidance to our participants including CV writing, interview preparation, and skills development.

  • Meeting and exceeding performance targets and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

Working Together

  • Collaborating with participants to shift their mindset and build the confidence they need to find and sustain work.

  • Engaging with local employers to identify job opportunities.

  • Signposting participants to internal and external stakeholders to address specific barriers such as health, housing, or financial challenges.

  • Promoting the Restart Scheme within the community, raising awareness of it's benefits and impact.

Being Fair, Open, and Honest

  • Providing inclusive support and advice to people from all backgrounds.

What’s in it for you?

A generous base salary (pro-rata for part time), and great flexibility with your working schedule, we offer training, development and progression opportunities. You will have access to the range of Reed in Partnership benefits, which include:

  • 25 days annual leave (pro-rata for part time) plus statutory bank holidays

  • Reed Pension Scheme

  • Award Winning Management & Leadership training

  • Professional & Personal Development Funds

  • Bi-annual pay reviews

  • Plus much more that can be found on our website.

The Employment Adviser role offers immense satisfaction of connecting people with the tailored support that they need to fulfil their potential. At Reed in Partnership, our values - Fair, Open & Honest, Take Ownership, and Work Together - guide everything we do. Join us in delivering services that make a real difference.

To be successful in this role, we are looking for someone with:

  • Ability to demonstrate coaching/mentoring experience and persuasion/influencing skills through previous work or social activities.

  • Experience of working in a customer facing environment (i.e. Customer Services, Hospitality, Social Care, Customer Services, Sales)

  • Experience of working in a fast paced, performance target driven environment.

title: AI Security Engineer
description:
Your influential mission. You will...

  • Review the AI systems and infrastructure, including local and cloud LLM deployments, gateways, vector stores, and agentic / MCP components, and provide clear recommendations on required hardening measures and areas for improvement.
  • Assess existing guardrails and controls, such as input/output filtering, prompt-injection defenses, rate limiting, and authentication, against industry best practice, provide recommendations to strengthen their effectiveness and drive the implementation of improvements and new controls to ensure the secure and responsible use of AI.
  • Advise on secure-by-design AI architecture, reviewing team designs and deployments against recognized frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001).
  • Recommend and prioritize hardening across the infrastructure behind self-hosted and cloud-based LLMs, and guide teams through remediation.
  • Evaluate the AI supply chain, such as model provenance, AIBOM/SBOM, dependency and artifact scanning, and provide recommendations to address gaps (Including Vibe Coded Applications).
  • Define standards, reference patterns, and best-practice guidance to ensure teams across Playtech build and operate AI securely.
  • Review logging, observability, and detection coverage for AI workloads mapped to frameworks such as MITRE ATLAS, and recommend enhancements to ensure the SOC can effectively monitor and respond across the full AI attack surface.
  • Assess identity, access, and secrets management for models, tools, and data, advising on least-privilege improvements.
  • Support compliance in a regulated environment with audit-ready assessments, evidence, and documentation.
  • Drive innovation within the team — Investigate and where possible implement Agentic AI usage within the unit, to optimize time consuming activities (Chatbots, automation with Hermes or n8n etc)

Components for success. You...

  • Hold valid and relevant Certifications or equivalent, verifiable experience in the field of Cyber Security and/or Information Technology.
  • Bring solid infrastructure and security engineering experience — Linux, networking, cloud, IAM, container security and automation.
  • Know your way around both self-hosted LLM deployment and cloud LLM platforms (e.g. Azure Foundry, Amazon Bedrock, Google VertexAI, Ollama, LMStudio etc).
  • Can review and assess AI systems against best practice and clearly advise teams on what to harden, improve, or remediate on an ongoing basis.
  • Have prior knowledge of LLM-specific threats: prompt injection, sensitive-data disclosure, data/model poisoning, excessive agency, insecure output handling, supply-chain risk and how to mitigate them.
  • Have knowledge of some of the various AI security frameworks and Guidelines — OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) and for Agentic Applications (2026), MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, CISA/NSA guidance, and the EU AI Act — and how to translate them into controls.
  • Have prior experience in guardrail implementation and design evaluation, including prompt-injection defense, output validation, and hallucination mitigation.
  • Had exposure to using infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Ansible) and CI/CD pipelines to make controls repeatable.
  • Have experience navigating, and working in regulated environments such as gaming, finance, or healthcare.
  • Have clear communication, presentation and collaboration skills — strong documentation skills and cross-team collaboration are central to this role.

You'll get extra points for...

Thrive in a culture that values...

  • Ownership, curiosity, and a proactive approach to solving complex security challenges
  • Continuous learning and the opportunity to grow into the role while working on AI security topics that are becoming increasingly important for the business.

SYSTEM SECURITY TEAM

You will be part of the System Security - Endpoint & Gateway team, collaborating closely with another System Security team focused on Data & Identity Security. You will work with team members including an AI Security Engineer focused on Workforce AI, System Security Engineers, and a Principal Security Engineer, while also collaborating with the Playtech AI Committee, other Playtech Security teams, the Application Security Team, and teams across the wider business.

Our Port and Marine Terminals group is currently made up of teams spread across North America, including New York, New Jersey, Boston, Jacksonville, Tampa, West Palm Beach, San Diego, San Franciso, Vancouver, Montreal, and Halifax. The group provides services for all phases of a project's life cycle, from planning through decommissioning including detailed design, construction, and operation. Our many achievements include container terminals, oil and gas facilities, dry bulk ports, marinas, coastal structures, wharves, jetties, naval facilities and cruise terminals. Stantec was recently ranked as a Top 10 Marine and Port Facilities engineering firm by ENR.

Your Opportunity

Our Ports and Marine Terminals group is growing throughout the United States. We are seeking an experienced technical lead and project manager to assist the overall North American team and to grow the team in Houston, Texas. As the Senior Principal, Ports & Marine Terminals team, you will leverage your experience to provide oversight and technical management to projects across North America and to grow the Texas practice managing the design and delivery of projects. You will play a pivotal role in expanding our client and project base and in efforts to position the firm to acquire new business in the Texas market and beyond.

In this position, you will have the opportunity to work as part of the PMT team of planners, engineers and technologists on multiple projects for a range of public and private sector clients. This is a great opportunity for a motivated, energetic individual who wants to challenge their abilities in a dynamic work environment.

Your role as a senior contributor on our professional consulting services team is to work independently on projects of high complexity, and as a leader of a team or project through all phases of a project lifecycle. You are responsible for developing and implementing an engineering discipline group equipped with up-to-date engineering and design tools and innovations, technical and supervisory capabilities, and operating procedures to successfully and efficiently execute projects and consulting services resulting in client satisfaction and on-time delivery.

Your Key Responsibilities

  • Develops project work plans and ensures execution through oversight and management of the project team. Evaluates, selects, specifies, and engineers all structural engineered systems or products for a project.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

  • Strong understanding of all phases of project document production and the relationship between drawings and specifications.
  • Strong knowledge of marine structural systems means and methods, materials, and industry standards.

title: Associate Engineer - B (Civil/Structural)
description:
Build your career while building NYC Public schools and impacting the learning environments of the next generation!

The SCA’s Architecture and Engineering Department is responsible for development of scope, design, and construction documents for new school buildings, additions, lease conversions and renovation work of existing schools for New York City’s approximately 1.1 million students. Our projects are intentionally and thoughtfully designed; positive impact design is at the forefront of all our projects.

Our In-House studio is a multidisciplinary practice that is responsible for designing some of the largest and most complex schools in our 1,500+ school portfolio as well as renovation work to existing schools. Our other two studios manage external consultants from design inception to completion. Our three studios are comprised of talented architects and engineers who are driven to deliver high quality custom designed, sustainable, and resilient public schools.

Come and join our continuing journey towards design excellence in the K-12 education sector. Be impactful!

Job Description Summary

The Associate Engineer - B (Civil/Structural) functions as a project or team leader usually under the supervision of a licensed engineer for the scope, design, and post occupancy of projects.

Job Description

Responsibilities include:

  • Review scope reports and construction documents that have been submitted to ensure they conform to all applicable SCA standards, specifications, building codes, laws, agency requirements, etc. and document deviations.

  • Conduct sites surveys, prepare field reports, punch lists, and deficiency reports to facilitate design decisions that meet the standards of NYCSCA.

  • Visually observe all aspects of substantially completed work at construction site using design drawings to determine if a contractor has met all the requirements of the project.

  • Create and edit the content of design drawings and specifications intended for contractual construction and bulletin documentation.

  • Coordinate site assignments with third party surveyors and contractors, determine existing conditions, prepare logs.

  • Compares conditions at the construction site to contract drawings and specifications during site visits/field observations at the site to assess the progress and quality of work.

  • Perform related tasks.

May perform duties of Associate Engineer - A:

  • Assist in conducting sites surveys and prepare field reports, punch lists, and deficiency reports to facilitate design decisions that meet the standards of NYCSCA.

  • Assist in the preparation and peer review of construction documents as part of the design phase of projects. (Reso A, CIP's and Capacity school projects).

  • Assist or lead in the preparation of scope reports for CIP's and Reso A projects (assignment may be discipline specific) and the assist review of contractor bids and submittals to verify they meet the minimum standards and specifications of the SCA.

  • Assist in monitoring the progress of the construction phase of the project.

  • Assist in addressing requests for information.

  • Perform related tasks.


There are four specialty areas for Associate Engineer A: (1) Electrical, (2) Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC), (3) Plumbing and Drainage, and (4) Structural.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Two Years of full-time experience serving as an Associate Engineer - A or a satisfactory combination of education and experience.

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or related fields.

Civil Service Classification: Competitive

Posting End Date: 08/10/2026

  • Appointment Rate: $74,128 - $104,294

title: Stores Credit Experience Advocate - Late Shift
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story.

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As a Digital Seller, you will guide customers through their shopping journey by handling inbound calls, chats, and emails for furniture, bedding, and fine jewelry. This role focuses on delivering a great customer experience while driving sales through relationship building, personalized recommendations, upselling, and cross-selling. You will help customers find the right solutions, resolve issues professionally, and make every interaction feel helpful and engaging. This is a hybrid role that includes regular in-office requirements.

Why This Role Matters

This role matters because it shapes how customers experience Macy’s through service, selling, and problem resolution. By listening carefully, understanding customer needs, and offering thoughtful solutions, you help create a personalized experience that builds loyalty and trust in the Macy’s brand. Balancing customer care with sales opportunities helps drive business results and makes each interaction more meaningful.

How Our Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues create genuine connections by starting every interaction with warmth and sincerity. They know that hospitality is a feeling—shown through a smile, a kind word, and intentional conversations that build trust and lasting relationships.
  • When mistakes happen, they apologize authentically listening with empathy, valuing the customer's experience, and committing to making things right.
  • They take the time to truly understand customer needs before acting. They take ownership in every situation, being proactive in finding solutions, offering helpful resources, and communicating clearly and confidently.
  • Their full attention is always on the customer. To reassure customers, they follow through with clarity and consistency, delivering on promises and making things right when expectations aren't met.
  • They know that excellence is shown by focusing on what matters most to the customer.

What To Expect

In this role, you will support customers by phone, chat, and email while handling questions, purchases, and issue resolution in a fast-paced environment. You will use selling skills to recommend products, offer solutions, and close sales in a natural, customer-focused way. Business needs may shift, so flexibility, dependability, and the ability to adapt quickly are important for success.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Create a welcoming experience by greeting customers warmly and showing appreciation for their business.
  • Guide customers to the right products by asking thoughtful questions, identifying their needs, and recommending relevant options.
  • Drive sales through personalized service, suggestive selling, upselling, and cross-selling across furniture, bedding, and fine jewelry.
  • Handle inbound calls, chats, and emails efficiently while resolving customer issues with empathy, professionalism, and urgency.
  • Partner with stores, suppliers, distribution centers, buyers, and leadership to resolve complex or urgent customer needs.
  • Bring consistency, sound judgment, and attention to detail to every interaction while adapting to changing business needs.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to deliver a customer-first experience in every interaction
  • Selling skills, including product recommendations, upselling, and cross-selling
  • Strong problem-solving, research, and decision-making skills
  • Comfort using multiple computer applications and dual monitors
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple tasks
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and across communication channels based on business needs
  • Regular, dependable attendance and punctuality

Nice to Have

  • One year of customer service or sales experience preferred
  • Product knowledge in furniture, bedding, fine jewelry, or similar categories
  • Experience in a fast-paced customer contact environment
  • Ability to handle complex customer situations with sound judgment and professionalism
  • Enthusiasm for fashion, home, and delivering exceptional customer care

Physical Activities You Will Perform:

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. Responsibilities include the ability to access and review written and electronic information, and to move within the work environment and interact with workplace materials as needed to carry out job responsibilities.
  • Frequently lift/move up to 10lbs.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

description:
Overview

If you're seeking more than just a job, join Heights Finance and kickstart your career!

Are you ready to make a difference in the world of consumer finance? At Heights Finance, a proud member of the Attain Finance family, we bring over 50 years of expertise in providing credit solutions across the U.S. and Canada. Our deep roots in the financial industry have empowered us to develop convenient, easily accessible financial services that meet our customers' growing needs.

Join a leading consumer credit lender that thrives on innovation and collaboration, where your contributions are truly valued. As part of Attain Finance, our portfolio includes distinguished brands like Cash Money®, LendDirect®, Heights Finance. Each brand is constantly evolving to better serve our customers.

Be part of a dynamic team that is shaping the future of consumer finance. Apply today!

Stories of Success

"I joined Heights Finance in 2010 as a CSR, with no prior experience in finance. Little did I know that this role would pave the way for a fulfilling career! Heights Finance genuinely values its team members and takes pride in promoting from within. Today, I am proud to serve as a District Manager, a position I moved into in 2021 – Also, a testament to the growth opportunities the company provides. The company offers excellent benefits, a set schedule that promotes work-life balance, and supportive leadership that ensures every team member feels valued. The company, also fosters an open culture, encouraging team members to share their ideas and suggestions. I truly love working here and am grateful for the incredible opportunities Heights Finance has provided."

~ Ashley S., District Manager - Alabama

"Since joining Heights Finance as a Branch Manager in 2013, I have enjoyed the benefit of internal transitions and promotions on multiple occasions. Transitioning from my original branch to a larger branch in a different demographic, to a middle-sized branch in a combination of demographics, assisted me with being prepared to take the next step in my career. As a result, of these experiences, I was qualified for a District Manager position in 2021. In 2024, I made a career change and with the support of my VPO, I was able to move into an Operations Trainer. During each transition, my supervisors worked to ensure I had the training, tools, and support needed to be successful and the level of camaraderie amongst my peers was unparalleled."

This is more than just a job—it’s a chance to grow your career, make a difference, and be rewarded for your success.

If you're a motivated, customer-focused professional with a passion for helping others and a drive to succeed, we want to hear from you. Join our team and let’s achieve success together!

  • Learn and Grow: Participate in a hands-on training program with one-on-one mentoring to build your skills and confidence.
  • Ensure Compliance: Follow all regulatory guidelines and company policies to protect customer information and company assets.

This is your opportunity to build a rewarding career with a company that values your contributions and supports your growth.

We’re looking for individuals who are passionate about customer service, eager to learn, and ready to grow in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

  • Customer Focus: A genuine desire to help others and provide top-tier service in every interaction.
  • Sales Mindset: Confidence in promoting products and services that meet customer needs.
  • Strong Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to build rapport quickly.
  • Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to think on your feet and offer creative solutions to customer challenges.
  • Adaptability: Willingness to learn new systems and processes in a dynamic environment.
  • Team Player: A collaborative spirit with a desire to contribute to team success.
  • Educational Background: High School diploma or equivalent required; college coursework or degree is a plus.
  • Industry Experience: Experience in customer service, sales, or consumer finance is preferred but not required—we’ll train the right candidate!

title: Lead Security Research Engineer
description:
Come work at a place where innovation and teamwork come together to support the most exciting missions in the world!

As a Lead Security Research Engineer, you will provide technical leadership for vulnerability research, exploit analysis, exposure validation, and vulnerability signature development across the Qualys security platform. You will lead initiatives to identify, validate, and prioritise security risks based on real-world exploitability, helping customers distinguish theoretical exposures from confirmed attack paths.

Responsibilities:

- Lead vulnerability research initiatives across operating systems, databases, enterprise applications, cloud services, container platforms, and network devices.
- Research newly disclosed, N-day, and actively exploited vulnerabilities.
- Lead the development of exploit-based exposure validation techniques to confirm real-world exploitability of vulnerabilities.
- Review technical designs, research methodologies, and code contributions to ensure quality and consistency.
- Partner with Engineering and Product teams to influence roadmap decisions and security content strategy.
- Design safe and controlled validation mechanisms that emulate attacker behavior without affecting production systems.
- Analyze vulnerability root causes, attack vectors, exploitability conditions, and potential business impact.
- Mentor and guide Security Research Engineers on vulnerability analysis, exploit analysis, and signature creation.
- Build validation logic capable of determining whether existing security controls such as WAFs, firewalls, EDRs, IPS, and compensating controls effectively prevent exploitation.
- Drive automation initiatives for vulnerability research, exploit validation, content generation, testing, and release processes.
- Establish best practices, coding standards, and quality guidelines for signature development.


Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (or equivalent experience).

- 8+ years of hands-on experience in vulnerability research, penetration testing, detection engineering, or security research.
- Deep understanding of TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SSH, SMTP, DNS, SSL/TLS, and modern web protocols.
- Strong expertise in vulnerability analysis, exploit development, and attack techniques.
- Extensive knowledge of operating systems, databases, web technologies, cloud environments, and enterprise infrastructure.
- Strong coding background.
- Experience with packet analysis, network troubleshooting, and protocol reverse engineering.
- Knowledge of OWASP Top 10, common attack techniques, and modern threat actor tactics.
- Excellent written, verbal, and technical communication skills.
- Demonstrated experience leading projects and mentoring technical teams.


Additional Plus Competencies:
Understanding of Lua (preferred), Bash, or Python.
Knowledge of Cloud Platforms (AWS, Azure, Oracle, etc.).

Experienced in the use of vulnerability scanners, IDS, and security tools.
OSCP, CISSP, or SANS GIAC certifications.

title: Warehouse Inventory and Logistics Coordinator
description:
We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Warehouse Inventory and Logistics Coordinator for our warehouse operations, inventory control, and fleet management. In this role, you will act as a central hub for incoming and outgoing materials, maintaining high standards of organization, safety, and inventory accuracy across our facility and fleet. Your primary focus will be coordinating the Suspended Material Area (SMA), executing Return Material Authorization (RMA) dispositions, performing incoming inspections, managing fleet upkeep, and maintaining inventory accurate records within our Workforce Management System.

The ideal candidate has at least 3 years of experience in warehouse control, inventory management, shipping/receiving, or logistics coordination. This person possesses exceptional organizational skills, a strong eye for detail, and thrives in a hands-on environment where maintaining systematic workflows and inventory accuracy is critical.

Core Responsibilities

1. Suspended Material Area (SMA) & RMA Management

● SMA Coordination: Maintain, organize, and monitor the Suspended Material Area (SMA) to ensure items are properly tracked and neatly organized.

● RMA Processing: Properly disposition items assigned to the SMA, including processing returns through standard Return Material Authorization (RMA) procedures, including proper inventory transactions.

● Aging & Tracking: Actively track all items in the SMA, monitoring dwell time to ensure materials are dispositioned in a timely manner and preventing unhandled backlog.

● Area Upkeep: Keep the SMA safe, clean, orderly, and clearly labeled at all times.

2. Shipping, Receiving & Incoming Inspection

● Receiving Inspection: Perform detailed incoming inspections to verify that physical shipments match vendor paperwork (packing slips) and order system specifications.

● Material Job Assignment: Accurately assign and stage incoming materials to the correct job upon receipt to support operational workflows.

● Shipping Execution: Package, document, and schedule outgoing shipments in alignment with company standards and delivery timelines.

● Parts Pickup Area: Maintain and clean the parts pickup area, ensuring it remains organized, accessible, and neat for internal team pickups.

3. Fleet Operations & Vehicle Maintenance

● Vehicle Status Monitoring: Monitor the overall status and health of the company fleet, tracking routine maintenance schedules and coordinating necessary service or repair needs as required.

● Garage Parking Safety: Maintain a safe, clear, and consistent parking pattern for all fleet vehicles stored in the garage facility.

● End-of-Life Dispositioning: Assist management in the evaluation, coordination, and disposition process for vehicles reaching their end of life.

4. Warehouse & Inventory

● Workforce Management System (WMS) Data Entry & Maintenance: Maintain inventory accurate records within the BuildOps Workforce Management System, supporting accurate counts and real-time tracking.

● Fleet Inventory Support: Support vehicle inventory processes, assisting with stock checks and material tracking across the fleet.

● Warehouse Coordination: Oversee general warehouse operations to maintain a neat, safe, and highly structured environment.

● Obsolete Inventory Disposition: Identify and properly disposition old, obsolete, or non-viable inventory to maximize space and operational efficiency.

Required Skills & Qualifications

● Experience: Minimum of 3 years of experience in warehouse coordination, shipping and receiving, inventory control, or logistics operations.

● Software Proficiency: Hands-on experience utilizing a Workforce Management System (WMS) or Inventory Management Software, preferably BuildOps or similar. Proficiency with basic inventory tracking platforms is required. Competency with Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel is required.

● RMA & Inspection Skills: Proven understanding of RMA workflows, return handling, and incoming material inspection practices against purchase orders and shipping manifests.

● Fleet Coordination: Prior experience monitoring vehicle service needs, coordinating fleet upkeep, or assisting with equipment/vehicle disposition.

● Organization & Detail: Outstanding organizational and spatial management skills, with a track record of keeping physical warehouses and staging areas neat, organized, and safe.

● Communication & Collaboration: Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively coordinate across operations, field teams, vendor logistics providers, and management.

description:
Space Electronic Warfare and Counterspace Specialist

The Opportunity:

With all the information available today, it takes a skilled intelligence analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government every day, we need an intel analyst like you to do just that. As a space electronic warfare and counterspace specialist, you use your specialized technical experience and your attention to detail to analyze data and operational scenarios, to give your client the actionable intelligence and context they need. If you have strong analytical skills and a problem-solving mindset, we have an opportunity to use those skills to support our national security leaders.


As an intelligence analyst on our team, you’ll help your client understand the space electronic warfare and counterspace requirements for this mission. Using your comprehensive understanding of various collection platforms, you’ll explore new data sources, develop effective queries, and combine information from disparate sources including national and DoW space systems. You’ll validate information and develop tradecraft as you build assessments for space operations and national system decisionmakers. As the authority on space EW and counterspace, your client will look to you for time-critical recommendations, often under pressure.


This is a chance to grow your expertise and broaden your skillset into areas like mission threats, growth, and operations support. You’ll share your expertise with other analysts through leadership and mentoring. We focus on growing as a team to deliver the best support to our customers, so you’ll have resources to learn new skills and tools.

Work with us as we provide the right information at the right time to support the critical needs of our national space leadership and warfighters.


Join us. The world can’t wait.

The position will be based in Zambezia.

description:
Overview

Greenleaf Behavioral Health Hospital is hiring an RN House Supervisor!

Available Schedules:

Full Time Night

Pay Range: $40.14 to $58.25 per hour (depending on years of experience)

Greenleaf Behavioral Health, is a leading Psychiatric Hospital and Treatment Center that is seeking passionate RN House Supervisors to work at our adolescent and adult facility in Valdosta, GA.

Responsibilities

​ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • ​Anticipates and effectively manage changes in census and acuity and allocates nursing resources based on measurement of patient acuity/care needed
  • ​Role models expectations related to customer service and demonstrates a sense of urgency related to the importance of patient safety
  • ​Enforce and interpret policies for the delivery of patient and resident care.

  • ​Document medical, behavioral health information and nursing care.
  • ​Administer medications and maintain records in accordance with company policies and procedures.
  • ​Assist in developing a plan of care with specific and measurable goals, objectives and interventions defining actions unique to each patient's needs. Assist in updating and revising the plan of care as goals/objectives are met or when the patient's condition changes.

​Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

  • ​BSN from accredited school of nursing preferred.

  • ​Greater than 1 year of experience as an RN strongly preferred.

  • ​1 year in psychiatric/recovery programs preferred.
  • ​Some experience as a charge RN or other leadership position strongly preferred.

​Current certification or license to practice within the state where the facility is located. CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).

title: Rental Return Agent
description:
Rental Return Agents er ansvarlig for at utleiebiler leveres tilbake på en rettidig og ryddig måte, og at de blir kontrollert og klargjort for neste utleie. Denne stillingen innebærer samhandling med kunder, behandling av leieavtaler og betalinger, og inspeksjon av kjøretøy. Denne stillingen krever vanligvis utmerkede kundeserviceferdigheter og evne til å jobbe i et miljø med høyt tempo.

Noen spesifikke ansvarsområder til en Rental Return Agent kan inkludere:

  • Hilse på kunder som returnerer leiebiler

  • Inspeksjon av kjøretøy for skader eller problemer, og dokumenter dem med passende verktøy og vurdere eventuelle nødvendige kostnader etter behov

  • Forklar alle sluttgebyrer til kunder og samle underskrifter på leiekontraktkvittering

  • Bistå med veibeskrivelse og reiseinformasjon

  • Utfør grundig inspeksjon av kjøretøy og sikre at kjøretøyene er klargjort for neste utleie

  • Føre nøyaktige journaler og fullføre papirarbeid

  • Løse kundeklager og problemer på en rettidig og profesjonell måte

  • Sikre at parkeringsplassen for leiebiler er organisert og godt vedlikehold

  • Sørge for at sikkerhets- og sikkerhetsprotokoller følges til enhver tid

Kvalifikasjoner / Ferdigheter:

  • Videregående vitnemål eller tilsvarende utdanningsnivå

  • Snakker og skriver engelsk flytende / på høyt nivå

  • Tidligere erfaring fra salg eller kundeservice, spesielt innen bilutleie, retail eller hospitality bransjen, gjerne 1-2 år

  • Gyldig førerkort med ren straffeattest

  • Åpenhet for fleksibel arbeidstid, inkludert helger

  • Dokumentert kommunikasjons- og mellommenneskelige ferdigheter

  • En teamorientert tilnærming

  • Bevist evne til å håndtere flere oppgaver og prestere godt i et hektisk arbeidsmiljø

  • En vennlig, optimistisk og proaktiv holdning.

Job Title:

Education Program Specialist, Evaluation & Assessment- Education Curriculum

Department:

Medicine | Education Curriculum

The Office of Medical Education in the College of Medicine oversees the development, implementation, evaluation, and accreditation of the Lead.Serve.Inspire. (LSI) curriculum for the Doctor of Medicine (MD) program. The LSI curriculum integrates foundational science with early patient interaction and longitudinal clinical practice, leveraging the resources of a comprehensive academic health center. The curriculum is structured into three parts across four years: Part One: Clinical Foundations (Years 1–2), Part Two: Clinical Applications (Year 3), and Part Three: Advanced Clinical Management (Year 4).

The MD program in the College of Medicine supports a traditional 4-year MD track, an accelerated 3-year primary care track, the medical scientist training program (MSTP), and the community medicine track (CMT).

Position Summary:

The Education Program Specialist on the Evaluation & Assessment (E&A) team plays a critical role in supporting and overseeing key assessment and evaluation functions in the pre-clerkship and clinical years of the LSI curriculum. This position collaborates with Academic Program Directors, the E&A Faculty Director and Program Manager, other faculty, and staff to ensure effective implementation, coordination, and continuous improvement of grading processes, course evaluations, accommodations with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and special projects.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Grading Meeting Support: Provides grading meeting coordination and support, including managing all CMT grading meetings; ensuring accurate and timely grade entry and reporting in compliance with program standards; collaborating with faculty and program leadership to resolve grading-related issues and maintain confidentiality.
  • Staff Supervision: Supervise program assistants responsible for proctoring coordination across all parts of the curriculum; serve as a proctor when needed to ensure secure and consistent exam administration; provide training, guidance, and performance oversight to maintain high standards of service.
  • Course Evaluation: Oversee the course evaluation process, ensure timely deployment and accurate data collection; supervise staff work related to evaluations and provide quality assurance; collaborate with faculty and leadership to analyze evaluation data and support continuous improvement.
  • ADA Accommodation Administration: Coordinate with Student Life and Disability Services (SLDS) to implement ADA accommodation for assessments and learning activities; increase support for Part 2 and Part 3 programs, ensuring compliance and equitable access; oversee ADA implementation and provide longitudinal support for students and program leadership; support digital accessibility needs within the program.
  • Special Project Support: Support ExamSoft transition from legacy to enterprise system, ensuring smooth implementation; assist with Part 2 curricular revitalization efforts and CMT expansion initiatives; contribute to curricular adoption of Association of American Medical Colleges Foundational Competencies for Undergraduate Medical Education and other strategic projects as assigned.
  • Departmental Support Provide coordination and administrative support for cross-functional projects and task forces aligned with the Office of Biomedical Education’s mission. Collaborate across teams to provide interim support, especially during peak periods, to ensure smooth program operations. Maintain regular in-person engagement to support learners and ensure continuity of service. Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
  • Four years of relevant experience required; four to eight years preferred

Preferred Qualifications:

Previous administrative experience desired. This position requires strong organizational, communication, and collaboration skills, along with technical aptitude, analytical thinking, adaptability, initiative, and attention to detail. The ability to work effectively with multiple stakeholders and teams is essential to ensure the smooth operation and delivery of the curriculum. Previous supervision experience preferred. Attention to detail and follow through, along with consistently meeting deadlines.

title: Bioanalytical Scientist
description:
We are seeking a bioanalytical assay scientist to support the development, optimization, and execution of immunology-based bioanalytical assays. The primary focus of this role will be cellular immunology methodologies used to characterize functional T-cell and B-cell subsets as well as innate immune responses in support of early vaccine programs. This position will also include routine laboratory and instrument maintenance and will be based in Springhouse, PA.

  • Independently execute complex cell-based and immunology-based bioanalytical assays, utilizing techniques such as flow cytometry, ELISpot/FluoroSpot, MSD, and Luminex platforms
  • Perform assay setup, sample processing, acquisition, data review, and first-line data interpretation with a high degree of technical rigor and attention to detail
  • Support assay development, optimization and qualification activities for nonclinical and clinical biomarker and immunogenicity applications
  • Conduct clinical sample testing for qualified bioanalytical assays
  • Troubleshoot assay performance issues, instrument challenges, reagent variability, and sample-related issues, and recommend scientifically sound corrective actions
  • Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot complex laboratory instrumentation, including flow cytometers and cell sorters, ELISpot/FluoroSpot readers, liquid handlers, and integrated robotic platforms
  • Prepare reagents, controls, and study materials and perform PBMC isolation and related cellular workflows as needed to support assay readiness and execution
  • Maintain accurate, complete, and inspection-ready records in accordance with SOPs, Good Documentation Practices, and applicable regulated laboratory requirements
  • Assist in drafting and reviewing SOPs, protocols, forms, reports, deviations, and other technical documentation to support compliant assay execution
  • Collaborate effectively with laboratory scientists, robotics engineers, project teams, management, and Quality partners to deliver high-quality data and meet program timelines
  • Work safely and compliantly in a structured laboratory environment, including adherence to BSL-2 practices and applicable GLP/GxP expectations

The site is not accessible by public transportation routes.

Minimum Requirements:

  • B.S. + 3-5 years, or M.S + 1-2 years relevant hands-on experience in Molecular Biology, Immunology, Cell Biology, Biology, Biochemistry, Biology, or related life sciences discipline
  • Required years of relevant hands-on experience in cell-based assays or immunology-based bioanalytical testing; prior contractor or industry laboratory experience preferred
  • Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Desired Experience:

  • Hands-on experience in cell-based assay execution and immunology-based bioanalytical methods in a laboratory setting
  • Foundational experience with one or more of the following platforms: flow cytometry, ELISpot/FluoroSpot, MSD, Luminex, and PBMC-based assays
  • Experience supporting assay development, optimization, qualification, validation, or sample testing activities
  • Strong familiarity of regulated laboratory practices, including GLP/GxP principles, Good Documentation Practices, deviation awareness, and controlled documentation
  • Experience operating complex laboratory instrumentation and maintaining clear maintenance and performance records
  • Sound scientific judgment, attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to recognize and appropriately escalate technical or compliance-related issues
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document work clearly and communicate effectively across technical and cross-functional teams
  • Ability to work independently, learn new techniques, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced, timeline-driven environment

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience analyzing flow cytometry data using specialized software platforms
  • Experience with statistical analysis, data visualization, or scripting tools such as R, Python, or similar platforms
  • Prior experience in a regulated bioanalytical or clinical laboratory environment, including support for assay qualification and sample testing
  • Experience with laboratory automation, liquid handlers, instrument integration, and Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS)

Position is full-time, Monday-Friday, generally 8 a.m. - 5 p.m., but may vary to meet the assay needs; overtime as needed. Candidates currently living within a commutable distance of Spring House, PA are encouraged to apply. The site is not accessible by public transportation routes.

  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid vacation and holidays

title: Smart Water & AMI Consultant
description:
AECOM seeking a skilled and experienced Smart Water & AMI Consultant to join our growing water utility practice. In this role, you will serve as a subject matter expert and trusted advisor to municipal and regional water utilities navigating complex AMI procurements, program deployments, and digital transformation initiatives. You will lead owner's engineer engagements, support procurement processes, and deliver technical and strategic guidance that helps utilities maximize the value of their metering investments.

This position is ideal for a seasoned professional who has worked inside a utility or directly alongside one - someone who understands the operational realities of meter-to-cash workflows, the vendor landscape, and the organizational dynamics that drive (or stall) large infrastructure programs.

This will be a hybrid position including a combination of both remote, in-office and travel, that can be based out of any AECOM office within the US.

Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

Program Advisory & Owner's Engineer

  • Lead owner's engineer engagements supporting utility clients through AMI vendor selection, pilot design, full deployment, and program close-out
  • Advise utilities on AMI system architecture decisions including Point to MultiPoint, RF mesh, cellular, LoRa Wan and hybrid communication technologies
  • Develop and manage AMI KPI frameworks to track performance against technical, operational, and financial benchmarks
  • Facilitate and lead steering committee meetings, technical workshops, and stakeholder sessions

Procurement & Vendor Evaluation

  • Draft and review RFPs, technical specifications, evaluation criteria, and contract language for AMI hardware, software, and services
  • Conduct structured vendor evaluations using quantitative scoring methodologies across technology, commercial, and operational dimensions
  • Perform cost-benefit analyses, total cost of ownership modeling, and rate impact assessments
  • Support contract negotiations between utility clients and AMI vendors

Technical Analysis & Strategy

  • Assess meter data management (MDM) systems and MDMS-to-billing integration readiness
  • Evaluate non-revenue water (NRW) programs and identify AMI-enabled leak detection and loss reduction strategies
  • Advise on IT/OT integration including SCADA, CIS/billing, GIS, and customer portal connectivity
  • Develop business cases for AMI investment aligned to utility drivers including water conservation, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance

Business Development & Thought Leadership

  • Support proposal development including technical approach, scope of work, and fee estimation for AMI pursuits
  • Contribute to white papers, conference presentations, and industry working groups (e.g., AWWA, WaterNow)
  • Build and sustain relationships with utility clients, technology vendors, and industry peers

Minimum Requirements:

  • BA/BS in engineering, Business, Environmental Science, Public Administration, or a related field + 6 years of experience working for or directly with water organizations in an AMI, metering, or smart water capacity or a demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
  • Experience with end-to-end AMI deployment or major metering infrastructure upgrade
  • Experience with the AMI vendor landscape including platforms such as Itron, Sensus, Neptune, Kamstrup, Master Meter, Badger Meter, and comparable systems
  • Experience with meter data management (MDM) systems and their integration with CIS/billing platforms
  • Ability/willingness to travel 25% - 50% of the time

Preferred Qualifications

  • Graduate degree in a relevant technical or business discipline
  • Experience working as an owner's representative or independent technical advisor on behalf of a utility client
  • Working knowledge of non-revenue water (NRW) concepts, water loss auditing, and AMI-enabled leak detection
  • Experience reviewing or drafting procurement documents including RFPs, technical specifications, and contract terms
  • Understanding of municipal utility drivers including rate structures, regulatory requirements, conservation mandates, and capital planning
  • Active participation in AWWA or similar industry organizations
  • Familiarity with AMI data analytics platforms and customer engagement portals (e.g., Itron Temetra, Badger BEACON, Xylem Vue)
  • Exposure to lead service line replacement (LSLR) programs and AMI's role in supporting compliance and community outreach
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent
  • Experience supporting utilities receiving IIJA/BIL, WIFIA, or SRF funding for AMI capital programs
  • Knowledge of water sector cybersecurity standards applicable to AMI and OT environments
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present complex technical topics to non-technical stakeholders
  • This position does not offer sponsorship for U.S. employment now or in the future
  • This position does not offer relocation assistance

title: Lead Water Resources Engineer/Sr. Modeler
description:
Lead Water Resources Engineer/Sr. Modeler


Brampton, ON


At EXP, we’re driven to provide innovative solutions for the world’s built and natural environments. As a team of engineers, architects, designers, scientists, creators, and a community of professionals, we bring diverse and talented people together to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Here, you join a team that leverages differences, harnesses their entrepreneurial spirit in an employee-owned company, that believes diversity is what gives us strength, seeks sustainable results and shares ambitions for each other, our clients, and the communities we are part of and serve. To be a part of EXP means to have your own experience, while staying connected to a global network of professionals, who believe we are a part of something bigger. Together, we are EXP.


Are you ready to design your future?


Be our next Lead Water Resources Engineer/Sr. Modeler!


Your work environment at EXP


We are seeking a highly experienced and motivated Senior Water Resources Engineer/Modeler to lead and support complex hydrologic and hydraulic modeling projects. The ideal candidate will have over 10 years of experience in surface water modeling, floodplain analysis, and water resources planning. This role involves technical leadership, project management, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions and will be working in our Infrastructure Group.


What a day at EXP has in store for you

  • Lead the development and application of hydrologic and hydraulic models (e.g., HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS, SWMM, MIKE, Info Works).
  • Conduct floodplain mapping, risk assessments, and mitigation planning.
  • Analyze surface water systems including rivers, streams, and urban drainage networks.
  • Interpret and present modeling results to stakeholders, clients, and regulatory agencies.
  • Prepare technical reports, proposals, and presentations.
  • Mentor junior staff and contribute to technical excellence across projects.
  • Collaborate with GIS specialists, engineers, and planners to integrate modeling with spatial analysis and infrastructure design.
  • Stay current with industry trends, regulatory changes, and emerging technologies.
  • Proposal writing and support the team during proposals.

What your experience looks like

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in civil engineering, Environmental Engineering, Hydrology, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 10 years of professional experience in water resources modeling.
  • Proficiency in industry-standard modeling software (e.g., HEC-RAS 2D, HEC-HMS, SWMM, MIKE, Info Works ICM).
  • Strong understanding of hydrologic and hydraulic principles, floodplain management, and stormwater systems.
  • Experience with GIS tools (ArcGIS, QGIS) and data integration.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proven ability to manage projects, meet deadlines, and work collaboratively.
  • Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation or eligibility is preferred.

Preferred Skills

  • Familiarity with provincial and federal water management regulations.
  • Experience working with municipalities, conservation authorities, or government agencies.
  • Experience with climate change impact assessments and resiliency planning.
  • Knowledge of scripting or automation tools (Python, MATLAB) for model enhancement.

This job posting is for an existing position vacancy within our organization.

title: Employment Adviser
description:
Reed in Partnership has been delivering public services since 1998. We are a British, family-owned company, whose mission has always been to positively transform people and their communities. This is reflected in our services, which we deliver to help people from all backgrounds and circumstances to change their lives for the better.

Pay Range

£29,000 - £30,000

Working Hours/Pattern:

Full-time, although we would be happy to consider applicants who are looking to work on a part time basis. If you would like to explore this further please discuss this with the talent partner for this role. Please note our ability to accommodate flexible working arrangements will vary from role to role, dependent on business requirements.

Job Description

Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others to fulfil their potential?

Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?

Then consider the role of Employment Adviser at Reed in Partnership!

Please note, internal applications for this role close on 04/07/2026.

Who we are:

Reed in Partnership's Employability Division aims to positively transform lives by helping individuals who are unemployed, economically inactive, or facing challenges such as health conditions, disabilities, or caring responsibilities to find sustainable employment. Through a wide range of tailored support services including one-to-one careers guidance, CV writing, interview preparation, and skills training, we have supported over 250,000 people on their journey into work.

Our Restart Scheme, funded by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), focuses specifically on supporting the long-term unemployed who are referred and mandated to the scheme by their local Job Centre Plus. We provide them with up to 12 months of personalised support to enter or re-enter the workforce.

What is the role about?

Employment Advisers are the front line of Reed in Partnership, directly contributing to our mission by supporting jobseekers (our participants), engaging with local employers, and promoting the benefits of the Restart Scheme within the local community. Our participants are the lifeblood of our business and providing them with an excellent service is at the very core of the Employment Adviser role.

Just some of your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Taking Ownership

  • Meeting with and supporting a caseload of long-term unemployed jobseekers, identifying their barriers and creating tailored action plans to progress them into employment.
  • Delivering personalised, one-to-one guidance to our participants including CV writing, interview preparation, and skills development.
  • Meeting and exceeding performance targets and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

Working Together

  • Collaborating with participants to shift their mindset and build the confidence they need to find and sustain work.
  • Engaging with local employers to identify job opportunities.
  • Signposting participants to internal and external stakeholders to address specific barriers such as health, housing, or financial challenges.
  • Promoting the Restart Scheme within the community, raising awareness of it's benefits and impact.

Being Fair, Open, and Honest

  • Providing inclusive support and advice to people from all backgrounds.

What’s in it for you?

A generous base salary (pro-rata for part time), and great flexibility with your working schedule, we offer training, development and progression opportunities. You will have access to the range of Reed in Partnership benefits, which include:

  • 25 days annual leave (pro-rata for part time) plus statutory bank holidays
  • Reed Pension Scheme
  • Award Winning Management & Leadership training
  • Professional & Personal Development Funds
  • Bi-annual pay reviews
  • Plus much more that can be found on our website.

The Employment Adviser role offers immense satisfaction of connecting people with the tailored support that they need to fulfil their potential. At Reed in Partnership, our values - Fair, Open & Honest, Take Ownership, and Work Together - guide everything we do. Join us in delivering services that make a real difference.

To be successful in this role, we are looking for someone with:

  • Ability to demonstrate coaching/mentoring experience and persuasion/influencing skills through previous work or social activities.
  • Experience of working in a customer facing environment (i.e. Customer Services, Hospitality, Social Care, Customer Services, Sales)
  • Experience of working in a fast paced, performance target driven environment.
  • Willingness to travel locally (e.g. to meet customers/employers).
  • A minimum of 2 A-Levels or an equivalent Level 3 Diploma.
  • GCSE English Language at a minimum of a Grade B (or equivalent Level 2 qualification). OR achievement of a Level 2 in Literacy Assessment at interview stage OR International Equivalents.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Fluency in more than one language

We aim to ensure that no candidate or employee receives less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or belief, age, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria.

title: Data Engineer, Specialist Technology Team (STT), Centralized Data & Analytics
description:
AWS Specialist Technology Team (STT) is the connective tissue between AWS's deep technical specialists, field teams, and customers—delivering L300+ technical expertise, mechanisms, and products that accelerate customer success and drive frictionless AWS adoption at scale. Our mission spans two fronts: we are fundamentally transforming how thousands of field team members access specialist knowledge through AI-powered, on-demand expertise across 30+ technical domains, and we build and ship customer-facing engineered solutions that accelerate AWS service adoption across industries.

Our portfolio spans AI-powered specialist knowledge systems (Specialist Agent, Knowledge Vault), hands-on engagement platforms (Workshop Studio), content quality and recommendation engines (Holmes), and go-to-market orchestration tools (Alchemy)—collectively enabling field teams to deliver high-quality technical engagements at scale. These products serve thousands of users across the AWS sales organization, generating rich signals about content effectiveness, engagement delivery, knowledge consumption, and field team productivity.

We are seeking a Data Engineer to join our newly formed centralized analytics team as one of the first Data Engineers on the team. This is a greenfield opportunity to build a data platform from the ground up—making foundational architectural decisions and directly influencing how an entire organization measures success and makes investment decisions. You will design, build, and operate scalable data pipelines that connect product telemetry, usage metrics, and business outcomes into a coherent, unified data ecosystem. Your focus will be squarely on engineering—building robust, scalable infrastructure and data models—while dedicated Business Intelligence Engineers on the team own the reporting, dashboarding, and stakeholder-facing analytics. This is not traditional reporting—you will be building the data backbone that powers intelligent, agent-driven analytics experiences (MCP tools, agentic retrieval systems) enabling stakeholders to intuitively access and consume data within their day-to-day workflows. The data you engineer will inform executive reviews, drive product strategy, and power the next generation of self-service analytics tools used by thousands of AWS field team members.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate scalable ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest product telemetry, usage events, and business outcome data from multiple heterogeneous sources across the STT product portfolio

- Architect and implement a centralized data platform using AWS-native technologies (Redshift, S3, Glue, Lake Formation, Lambda, Athena) that serves as the single source of truth for organizational analytics

- Build and maintain data models that connect product usage signals to business outcomes (e.g., content effectiveness → field engagement → pipeline progression → revenue impact)

- Develop data infrastructure supporting AI/ML pipelines and agentic systems, including MCP tools and natural-language data access layers

- Implement data quality frameworks with automated monitoring, alerting, and validation to ensure accuracy and reliability as the platform scales

- Build self-service data products with clear SLAs, documentation, and governance that reduce ad-hoc request burden and empower stakeholders to answer their own questions

- Partner with Applied Scientists and SDE teams to provide clean, well-modeled data for agent evaluation frameworks, retrieval quality measurement, and content effectiveness scoring

- Establish data contracts, lineage tracking, and catalog metadata to support discoverability and trust across the organization

- Operate with a high bar for operational excellence—owning on-call, monitoring pipeline health, and proactively resolving data freshness or quality issues before they impact consumers

- Contribute to the evolution from static dashboards toward agentic data systems by building the foundational data layers that AI agents query and reason over

About the team
You will be joining a high-growth engineering organization at the forefront of applying generative AI and agentic technologies to transform how AWS field teams operate. The centralized analytics team is being built from the ground up—you will be one of the first two Data Engineers on the team, working alongside Business Intelligence Engineers, a Senior BD, an Applied Scientist, and a TPM. You will make foundational architectural decisions that define how the platform will be built, scaled, and operate for years to come. The pace of innovation is high, the problems are ambiguous, and the impact is measured across thousands of field team members and the customers they serve. This role offers the opportunity to shape foundational architecture decisions and influence how an entire organization consumes and acts on data.

About AWS
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

title: Flight Control & Dynamics Engineer
description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Harmattan AI is pushing the boundaries of high-speed autonomous flight, where control has to hold up at the edge of the envelope. Getting that right across a family of airframes is one of the most demanding parts of the flight software.

As a Flight Control & Dynamics Engineer, working out of Lausanne, Paris, or Zurich, you will own control law design and the system identification that feeds it, setting the control standard as the team grows. You will weigh classical against learning-based methods, from tuned control laws to reinforcement-learning policies trained in simulation and flown on hardware, and decide what actually flies.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • System Identification: Design excitation maneuvers and fit airframe models from flight data, with quantified error bounds.

  • Control Law Design & Tuning: Inner rate and attitude loops through outer position loops, with allocation, gain scheduling, and manual or automated tuning across the airframe family and flight envelope.

  • Sim-to-Real: Keep the in-house simulator faithful to the identified model, so control developed in simulation transfers to the aircraft.

  • Model Consumption: Turn the stability derivatives and coefficient tables from Aerodynamics into flying control.

  • Flight Test & Diagnosis: Verify across simulation, SITL, and HITL, including Monte Carlo campaigns, then fly and iterate from logs.

  • Mentorship: Depending on seniority, support the team by mentoring junior control and GNC engineers.

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

  • Educational Background: A strong academic record with a degree in aerospace, controls, robotics, or a related STEM field. A practical track record matters more than the specific degree.

  • System Identification & Control: Proven, hands-on identification and control on multirotor or fixed-wing platforms, validated in flight, with depth in at least one of MPC, INDI, or geometric control.

  • Embedded Realization: Real-time control implementation on constrained targets, split cleanly between a microcontroller and a companion computer.

  • Learning-Based Control: Familiarity with reinforcement learning and simulation-based training, and the judgment to know when a learned policy beats a classical design.

  • Professional Attributes:

    • Empirical and hardware-honest, disciplined about experiments and validation, grounded in real flight data.

    • Communicates clearly, able to present control and test results to engineers and senior stakeholders.

    • Thrives under pressure in a fast-paced environment with a no-task-is-too-small mentality.

  • Bonus: Multi-airframe or hover-to-cruise transition experience.

  • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI's mission of providing a defensive edge to allied nations through ethical, high-impact technology.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.
